title: The Core Issue: Overheating & Constant Crashing I
body:
I am extremely disappointed with the thermal performance of this laptop. Despite its high speed in basic tasks, it fails miserably under any sustained workload.
The Experience:
I attempted to render a standard 1.5-hour video at only 480p resolution. Even with such a low-resolution task, the laptop consistently crashed and shut down completely upon reaching the 30-50% mark. The left side of the chassis becomes dangerously hot while the right side remains cold, indicating a major flaw in internal heat distribution.
The Cooling Struggle:
In an attempt to fix this, I invested in two different types of external coolers:
A standard Takros laptop cooler (which did nothing).
A high-end, high-speed Gaming Turbofan cooler (DEPGI) designed for maximum pressure.
Even with the gaming cooler running at maximum speed (3500 RPM) and positioned directly under the CPU hot spot, the laptop still suffered from "Heat Soak" and crashed. The internal cooling system is simply not capable of handling more than 30 minutes of continuous processing.
Verdict:
This laptop is fine for watching YouTube or light office work, but it is useless for video editing or any production tasks, even at low resolutions like 480p. If you plan to do any work that requires the CPU to run for more than a few minutes, stay away from this model. The sleek design is not worth the constant thermal failures.

title: Great All-in-One Laptop for School & Work
body:
I purchased the HP OmniBook X Flip 2-in-1 (16", AMD Ryzen AI 5 340, 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD) on 02/14/26 from the Flowood store, and I’ve honestly been really impressed with it so far.
One of my favorite features is the 2-in-1 flip design. The ability to completely fold it back into tablet mode is incredibly convenient, especially when I’m switching between typing assignments and just browsing or reading. It feels versatile without sacrificing performance.
I primarily use this laptop for school and working from home, and it handles both effortlessly. Whether I’m running multiple tabs, working on assignments, or managing day-to-day tasks, it has more than enough power and capacity. The 16GB of memory really makes a difference with multitasking.
The 16” 2K touchscreen is another highlight—everything looks sharp and clear, and the touch functionality is smooth and responsive. It just feels like a premium experience overall.
If I had to sum it up, this laptop is a great balance of performance, flexibility, and design. It’s perfect for anyone who needs something reliable for productivity but also wants the convenience of a convertible device.
Highly recommend!

title: HP OmniBook X's stamp of approval
body:
HP OmniBook X Flip 16” 2-in-1 (Ryzen AI 5 340, 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD) — Honest Review
I picked up the HP OmniBook X Flip 16-inch 2-in-1 during Black Friday and I’ve been using it daily for work, multitasking, and content creation. Overall, this machine is solid.
Performance
This laptop handles real work. I run multiple apps at once — browser tabs, documents, spreadsheets, design tools — and it stays smooth with almost no lag. The Ryzen AI 5 340 paired with 16GB of RAM is more than capable for everyday business use and creative tasks.
Touchscreen & 2-in-1 Design
The touchscreen is on point. Responsive, accurate, and smooth whether I’m scrolling, editing, or flipping it into tablet mode. The flip design makes it easy to switch between laptop and tablet depending on how I’m working.
Display
The 16-inch 2K screen looks great overall, but brightness is the one area that could be better. Indoors it’s fine, but in bright rooms or near windows it can feel a little dim. Not a deal breaker, but definitely noticeable.
Storage & Build
The 512GB SSD is fast and gives plenty of room for files, programs, and projects. Boot times are quick and everything loads clean. The Meteor Silver finish looks clean and professional and the build feels solid.
Battery & Everyday Use
Battery life easily gets me through a full workday with mixed use. It’s become my daily driver for business tasks, writing, and light design work without any issues.
Final Verdict
This is a powerful, reliable 2-in-1 that delivers where it matters: speed, multitasking, and versatility. The only downside is the screen brightness, but everything else more than makes up for it.
If you want a large, responsive touchscreen laptop that can handle real work without slowing you down, this one is worth it.

One of the best 2-in-1 laptops I’ve ever used

The HP OmniBook X Flip truly exceeded my expectations. The 16” 2K touch display is stunning—sharp, bright, and very responsive. Whether I’m working, watching content, or using it in tablet mode, the screen quality makes a huge difference.

Performance is smooth and fast thanks to the AMD Ryzen AI 5 340 processor. Multitasking feels effortless, and the Copilot+ AI features actually add real value for productivity. With 16GB RAM and a 512GB SSD, everything loads quickly and runs without lag.

I also love the 2-in-1 design. The hinge feels solid, switching between laptop and tablet modes is seamless, and the Meteor Silver finish looks premium and professional. Battery life has been excellent for my daily use, easily lasting through work and entertainment.

Overall, this laptop offers an outstanding balance of performance, design, and innovation. HP really nailed it with this model, and I’d confidently recommend it to anyone looking for a powerful, modern, and versatile laptop.

title: So much better

Bought my first laptop (brand name). Display seemed ok. Boot up speed faster than my old desktop. Keyboard meh, but I am no typist. But, it wouldn't update through the initial setup. Had to update manually. Then the battery life...4 hours of streaming or just surfing and battery below 10%. Charged and drained many times. Still 4 hours. Returned that thing.
 Went to BB. Talked to Ty. They had a great deal on an HP laptop/tablet. Absolutely no comparison. Same memory and drive size. Upgraded chipset. Onboard AI. Better sound. Same price, vivid display, fast boot, awesome keyboard (with a backlight that actually helps). Battery lasts almost 10 hours. Oh, and it doesn't get hot just surfing.
 Would highly recommend an HP omnibook flip. If that's not what you are after, talk to Ty, get set up.

title: Decent budget laptop if no other options.
body:
The laptop itself has good build quality, good speakers, a big track pad, and great battery life; however that's as far as the complements go for me. 

There's no gap between the keys and despite being a 16" laptop, the keyboard lacks a numpad. It's very easy for crumbs to get stuck underneath the keys and not easy at all to get out. The laptop gets surprisingly hot during normal web browsing. The mouse cursor is not smooth at all while browsing. The screen has several unevenly lit areas. On the topic of the screen, it's too heavy for the hinges. Whenever I open the laptop screen past ~120°, the screen begins to slowly drop down under its own weight. It's not ideal for working on while on one's lap.

When I first booted up the laptop, the screen did not post. I'll be returning this laptop and searching for another.

It'll be enough for schoolwork, but not great for much past that. For $400 I'd say it's worth it, but I wouldn't spend any more than that.

title: Great style, poor execution
body:
Tl;dr Don’t purchase this laptop, unless you are literally doing the most basic of the basic, or incredibly simple, work tasks, don’t expect to really be able to run even the most basic and simple games without extreme leg, overheating, the fan’s going absolutely haywire, and the computer shutting down… Also be aware That the windows hello feature on this particular device is broken as mess
-
So at first, I thought this laptop seemed pretty great, seemed to run very quietly, loved the fact that I could flip, and I could draw and stuff on it, loved how sleek and nice it looked, however… I realized that once you tried to do any sort of task other than scroll through the web, the fans go into overdrive, and it overheats-
Not only that, the windows yellow feature is constantly breaking… Either constantly telling you that your pin is no longer working and that you have to reset it but then just giving you error, error code after error code, and within about two weeks of having it, the Face ID feature completely stopped working. No matter how many times I tried to reset it or use the codes sent through my email to reset Windows, it just wouldn’t work, even if the computer was fully up-to-date, when trying to open the WebCam I realized that it just didn’t work… Like, completely black screen. Yes, the WebCam is enabled, and the laptop has gone through no trauma, so it makes no sense that the facial recognition feature as well as the camera itself just decided to quit the job.
I have a few old laptops from high school that genuinely function better than this computer, but they are so old they can’t really run any sort of games whatsoever, so I purchased this laptop with the intent of playing some games with… Not extreme demand.
This laptop had a difficult time running Stardew valley… Stardew valley… it would overheat and lag on a game that has so little demand to it.
I tried a couple different games that require very little, such as that, fields of mistria, and Palia online as well- within the first very few months of having this computer I realized that it was artifacting, I’m not the tech expert, but my boyfriend is. He loves building PCs and he’s been obsessed with gaming and computers his whole life and he’s the one that told me that it seems like there are a lot of issues with this laptop.
I’m not sure if I just got a model with a lot of issues or… I have no idea. 
Like I said, I purchased this laptop because they reviews seemed to be overall positive if you were on the lower end of gaming and not expecting something insanely crazy for such a low price, but honestly for this price, and to only be able to scroll the web and not much else without the computer overheating and saying, bye-bye… Way overpriced. This laptop is basically a phone that you can run games on if you want to risk destroying the device you’re actually on (the laptop) the screen size is nice, and when it actually functions the way it should, I think it could be fantastic, but like I said, I’m not sure if I just got a model that happened to have several issues going on with it or what, because I love the design, I love how it feels, I love how beautiful the screen is, and the keyboard and everything about the design, and even a lot of the features, however, the way the laptop itself actually RUNS when doing anything aside from the MOST basic tasks needs some serious improvement. Lol 
I don’t usually write reviews, but because I’m not very technologically illiterate, I thought I might help somebody else out that is on the fence about this and knows as little as I do… I wouldn’t really recommend this, definitely dig deeper and talk to people that are more educated and do more research. I did quite a bit, but obviously not enough lol I thought this could handle the basics but it seems like it really can’t

title: Sweet Spot for Value
body:
Got it for a great deal when it was marked down during Black Friday; Further marked down because it was an open-box item. The laptop has worked without a hitch for university level workloads. Laptop ran without a hitch running MATLAB and Keysight ADS circuit software, all while listening to Spotify and having a few browser tabs open. I think most people that aren't expecting professional-grade performance will be more than happy with the Ryzen 6-core and 16 GB of RAM. While you may be able to find some more budget-oriented laptops for $100-150 cheaper with similarly performing specs, the jump in build and screen quality is a worthwhile upgrade. 

My only concern for the laptop is the implementation of AI features. As far as my understanding goes, the neural processing unit (NPU) is used for some extraneous tasks like blurring your background in a video call or creating closed captions. I ended up disabling the NPU in task manager, freeing up over 1 GB of reserved RAM. Given that the RAM is not upgradable, the NPU coupled with Windows 11 tend to drift into the >80% usage region in task manager.

No laptop is perfect, but this laptop performs very well for the money. I would recommend this laptop if you're a student or someone that just wants a nice Windows laptop for everyday tasks with a little more oomph on reserve.

title: Good product
body: I recently purchased the flip x laptop and have been thoroughly impressed with its performance and, especially, its versatile design. This laptop successfully bridges the gap between a high-performing work machine and a flexible, portable tablet. ​The Flip Feature: A Game Changer ​The standout feature is undoubtedly the 360^ circ hinge. The ability to effortlessly transition between Laptop Mode, Tent Mode (perfect for watching videos on a plane or small desk), and Tablet Mode has significantly enhanced my workflow and entertainment. The hinge feels sturdy and well-engineered, giving me confidence that it will stand up to frequent use. In Tablet Mode, the touchscreen is responsive and accurate, making it great for light browsing and media consumption. ​Performance: Snappy and Reliable ​In terms of raw power, this laptop is a beast. Powered by a AMD Ryzen 5 Ai processor and  16GG of RAM, multitasking is a breeze. I've been running demanding applications like  Photoshop and a dozen Chrome tabs / large spreadsheets and video conferencing simultaneously without any noticeable slowdowns or stuttering. ​Speed: Boot-up is nearly instantaneous thanks to the SSD storage. ​Graphics: [Optional - only if relevant] The integrated/dedicated graphics light gaming / high-resolution video editing surprisingly well. ​Design & Build Quality ​The overall aesthetic is sleek and modern. The chassis feels premium to the touch, and the weight is manageable for a flip-style device. The Full HD / 4K display is bright and the colors are vibrant, though I would perhaps wish for slightly thinner bezels / a little more brightness when working outdoors. ​Minor Drawbacks ​No device is perfect, and I have a couple of minor gripes: ​Battery Life: While good, it's not phenomenal. Under heavy load, I get about  5-6 hours before needing a charger. ​Port Selection: I sometimes miss having a dedicated Ethernet port / full-size SD card slot. However, the  USB-C / Thunderbolt] ports offer great connectivity with a dock. ​The Verdict ​The FLIP X 2 in 1 delivers on its promise of combining excellent performance with unmatched flexibility. If you're looking for a powerful machine that can easily adapt to different scenarios—from a serious work laptop to a relaxed tablet for movie night—this is an outstanding choice. Highly recommended for students, professionals, and anyone who values versatility.

title: Good but comes with SEVERAL underlying issues
body:
Pros: 
- Good for general work
- Large screen with decent quality
- Performance is fair
- handles basic tasks well

Cons:
- The laptop gets stuck in "tablet mode" taskbar forever, and there's no way to fix it (not that I know of). The only band-aid fix for this is to check off "Optimize taskbar for touch interactions when this device is used as a tablet" in settings, so you can never get the tablet taskbar again unless you check the option back on. (So what this means is you only get 2 options for your taskbar overlay for your "2-in-1" laptop: Windows 11 desktop taskbar or Tablet Windows taskbar, no in between, no changing taskbar setups automatically when you actually want to go into tablet mode, just one or the other). Additionally, it never automatically adjusts the orientation of the screen anymore, which wasn't a problem in the beginning; this is a big issue when you want to use it as a tablet. Apparently, there's supposed to be an option to disable "rotation lock," but there is literally no option for that to be found.
- Keyboard is horrific to use (but you'll eventually get used to it)
- The little padding at the bottom of the keyboard will create permanent scratches/marks on your screen. (circled in red in picture)

Conclusion: 
Not worth the base price of $800; the maximum you should spend on it is $500 on sale, plus you will run into a lot of issues if you want to use this laptop as a tablet. Even at the price of $500, it's still not getting what you paid for when half the features break or just don't work.

title: Great tablet experience for a 2 in 1 laptop
body:
The best 2 in 1 flip experience from the most reliable laptop brand names out there. This laptop has served me as a productivity master piece. The 2 in 1 makes it so that I don’t have to consider getting a tablet as this more than enough makes up for it.
I have been consistently using it for graphics design with a Metapen 2 which works with 4092 pressure points. 
My daily productivity and university tasks requiring AI were handled smoothly so definite packed on the processor side.
The poly studio speakers are something that I can’t complain about at this price point as it more than makes up enough for its price, should definitely consider playing around with an equalizer as they are decent for music and movies. The laptop is on the heavier side for something so thin but it is to be expected at this level of engineering. The display albeit being an IPS panel does a very good job representing the colors accurately, the only drawback is missing the deep blacks of an OLED, but at this price point this the best built 2 in 1 laptop.

I could not face more hours on the phone and text with tech support, so after a short time with them again for a recurrence of the same problem, I used the onboard diagnostic and got it to work for a little longer.  So, have been limping along. The sound will work if I restart the device immediately before I need to use the sound, like right before a Zoom meeting!  I live a a couple of hours away from a Best Buy store, and reaching them by phone has become more difficult as they do not allow customers to call the store directly anymore. title: HP Omnibook Flip 16" review
body:
The new Omni is quite a machine for the money retailing at $849. Lots of positive things about it, solidly made, the Ryzen 5 CPU is adequately fast for the casual user the display is very nice, has touch screen and backlit keyboard adding premium value and more usability to your purchase. Battery life is good. The stereo sound speakers are very nice. On sale I paid $551 which for a backlit keyboard machine was a good price. Best buy doubles the factory 1 year warranty to 2 years, that is exceptional and makes it worth buying at this retailer.  The Best buy tech chat was efficient and was able to help me with set up questions to their credit!

Cons:  The machines a little heavy at 4.2 pounds, but that means its more solidly built too. 

The keyboard is not the best for my typing with the caps key set too close to the "A" key for my taste, but I believe in time I will adapt to the new feel.

There is no SD card slot of any kind, which I miss, but you can just use a USB card adapter to overcome this deficiency.

Those are the only negatives I have, its overall a great machine and I am happy with my decision to purchase this unit. I expect it to last a long long time as HP is known for its longevity and is makiong a very nice quality machine !

title: I wanted new tech for a good price
body:
HP Omni book X-Flip Laptop - This was available at the time with good holiday pricing. I am more of a Dell person. I like their warranty onsite service . The ads for their laptops and Lenovo was listing older tech. I wanted USB-C 2.0 or better. 

This laptop had better display resolution as well along with 6E wireless. The processor speed isn’t up there with the other high end processors, but I am a retired pc and server service person, and more interested in home business use and browsing now.

The OS is Windows Home 11. I’m use to the Pro version, so I will see how limited my options are.
The battery life is rated in the 21 hours + range.

 I picked up a USB-C dock with Ethernet and SD and micro sd card and a 220w USB-c charger and additional cable to push the 100w dock and to charge the HP Omni book X-Flip Laptop. 

Setup was very easy and straightforward. I only wish that I had a backup on iCloud first. The process would have gleaned over my data effortlessly. I do have a separate backup on hdd and SD card so I did that. I will setup the iCloud backup later for this laptop. 

Purchasing this laptop was easy and I upgraded to the BestBuy Plus membership as a bonus freebee. I had a base membership before. 

I can’t speak for HP reliability yet since it is too early since the Labor Day weekend purchase. 

It looks great though ! I am sure that  this laptop will last me for a long while more.

title: My HP OmniBook X Flip is a Masterpiece
body:
I recently upgraded to the HP OmniBook X Flip 2-in-1, and after using it for a few weeks, I can confidently say it's one of the best tech purchases I've ever made. This isn't just a laptop; it's an incredibly versatile tool that excels in every scenario.

Stunning Design and Display: The Meteor Silver finish is sleek, professional, and feels premium. The star of the show, without a doubt, is the 16-inch 2K touchscreen. The resolution is incredibly sharp, colors are vibrant, and the touch responsiveness is flawless. Whether I'm editing photos, watching movies, or just browsing the web, the visual experience is immersive and beautiful. The anti-reflective coating is also a huge plus, making it usable even in brightly lit rooms.

Unmatched Versatility: The 2-in-1 flip design is where this device truly shines. I use it in:

· Laptop mode for serious work and writing.
· Tent mode for watching shows or following a recipe in the kitchen.
· Tablet mode for reading, sketching, or browsing with a stylus (sold separately). This flexibility means it seamlessly adapts to my day, replacing both my old clunky laptop and my tablet.

The "Copilot+ PC" AI Experience: This is the future, and it's incredible. The integrated NPU (Neural Processing Unit) and Ryzen AI 5 work silently in the background to make everything smoother. Features like enhanced voice clarity on calls, automatic framing for video conferences, and the ability to easily access Windows Copilot make my workflow more efficient. It feels like I have a smart assistant built directly into the hardware, anticipating my needs and optimizing performance.

Impressive Performance: Don't let the slim design fool you—this machine is powerful. The AMD Ryzen AI 5 processor, coupled with 16GB of RAM, handles everything I throw at it with ease. From having dozens of browser tabs open while streaming music and working on a large document, to light photo editing, there is zero lag. The 512GB SSD is blazingly fast, booting up in seconds and launching applications instantly.

Battery Life is a Game-Changer: HP's claims are not exaggerated. I easily get a full day of use on a single charge, often with power to spare. For a student or professional who is constantly on the move, the freedom from constantly hunting for an outlet cannot be overstated.
